name: Work Authorization and Residence Card (Employer-Sponsored)

requirements.blocker_text: Two separate authorizations are required: a carte de sejour (issued by the General Directorate of National Police, mandatory for stays over 90 days under Ordinance No. 2025-02, Article 5, valid 1-2 years and renewable) and a distinct work authorization from the Ministry of Employment, Labor and Social Protection, required before exercising paid employment. The employer must submit an 'attestation de non-disponibilite de competences locales' (attestation that no qualified Nigerien worker is available), an employment contract reviewed by the Labor Inspectorate, and pay an employment tax on foreign workers. Processing takes 15-30 working days. The mining sector reportedly caps foreign workers at 20% of a company's workforce with mandatory local-staff training, though this figure could not be independently confirmed against a primary legal text in this build. ECOWAS/CEDEAO citizens benefit from simplified procedures and multi-year residence permits.
requirements.fix_path: Have the employer secure the non-availability attestation and submit the work-authorization application to the Ministry of Employment, alongside the separate residence-card application to the police.

evidence_required.document: Residence card application (separate from work authorization)

outcome.duration_length: residence card 1-2 years, renewable; work authorization duration tied to contract

sources.title: Africarrieres (immigration/HR consultancy guide) -- dual permit system, non-availability attestation, mining-sector quota (unconfirmed), processing timeline
